_readme: TRELLIS.2 makes the product turntable from one real photo, so a product is rendered and never drawn.
No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
Draft: every entry is status draft until the owner approves it.
label: TRELLIS.2 4B (image to 3D)

limits.output: PBR GLB plus a preview video
limits.gpu: NVIDIA, at least 24 GB; tested on A100 and H100

house.use: builds the product turntable from one real photo
house.product_rule: the product is never drawn: a render of the 3D model is the picture (product-from-3D-model rule)

inputs.name: image
inputs.what: The one picture the model is built from.
inputs.we_send: the cleanest whole-product photo, nothing cut off, plain background

inputs.name: alpha
inputs.allowed: stored but inactive until connected in the 3D tool

structure.rule: Give it one clean, whole picture of the product; the model builds everything else from it.
structure.ours: kit photo chosen by the product check

structure.rule: Read the label on the turntable: a build can warp text; compare against the real photo before the model is used.
1024 builds in about 17 s on an H100; use 1536 only when the label is unreadable at 1024.
The export is opaque; if the cut-out matters, connect the alpha in the 3D tool.
structure.ours: turntable renders on a plain set

structure.rule: Pictures of the product come from renders of this model or the real photo, never drawn.
It needs a 24 GB NVIDIA GPU on Linux; on the Mac it runs through the door that has one.
structure.ours: door local means the worker that has the GPU

avoid.text: Expecting it to merge several photos: it takes one.
A photo with the product cut off: the missing part is invented.
A photo with a smear or reflection on or behind the product.
Using the turntable without comparing the label to the real photo.
Running it on a laptop without the GPU.
